name: XCath Iris
description: The XCath Iris is a teleoperated triaxial neuro-endovascular robotic platform developed by [XCath](/company/xcath) for intracranial vascular navigation, cerebral aneurysm embolization, and mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke. The bedside subsystem consists of a mobile cart with a positioning arm supporting a sterile cassette drive mechanism that provides sub-millimeter axial translation and rotation of standard commercial guidewires, microcatheters, aspiration/guide catheters, and treatment devices, as well as XCath's ElectroSteer electrically deflectable Nitinol guidewire. Controlled under fluoroscopic guidance from a radiation-shielded physician workstation locally or over long-distance network links, the system completed first-in-human intracranial brain aneurysm procedures in November 2025 and a remote telerobotic mechanical thrombectomy across 120 miles in Panama in March 2026.

lifecycle.note: Completed first-in-human intracranial aneurysm and remote telerobotic stroke thrombectomy trials in Panama; granted FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and accepted into the FDA TAP program in 2026.
